own_solution.law: For a uniform lossless transmission line, Z0 = sqrt(L_total/C_total) = 50 Ω. The launched voltage is V+ = E Z0/(Rs + Z0). At the load, ΓL = (RL − Z0)/(RL + Z0) = 0.5, so VL = V+(1 + ΓL) = 10 V. Adding 42 Ω at the source gives VL = 10(50)/(25 + 42 + 50) × 1.5 = 250/39 V.
assumptions: The cable follows the ideal uniform lossless transmission-line model.
The switched source applies a constant 10 V emf through its stated resistance.
The independently powered lamp has no electrical connection to the cable circuit.

defect_reasons.rendering_not_minimal: TBEAE and T0205 specify only a 'small resistor', whereas their numerical counterparts TAB4E and T8F3D specify 42 Ω, violating the requirement that variants preserve the same stated number and unit.

notes: The base physics and each individually augmented problem are well-posed; invalidity concerns the required variant matching. For either length sentence, L′ = L_total/ℓ and C′ = C_total/ℓ, so ℓ cancels from Z0 = sqrt(L′/C′). The first transit time is sqrt(L_total C_total) = 0.5 μs. The earlier-test resistors are absent from the present circuit. Neither unspecified resistor value affects the target, but the numerical matching requirement still fails.
